title: Network Service Port Registry
spec: Write a module to retrieve standard default network ports. Implement a function `get_default_port(service_name)` that uses an `if/elif` chain to map the following service strings to their integer ports: 'http_alt' -> 8080, 'https_alt' -> 8443, 'mysql' -> 3306, 'postgres' -> 5432, 'redis' -> 6379, 'mongo' -> 27017, 'memcached' -> 11211, 'rabbitmq' -> 5672. If the service is unknown, return 65535. Example: `get_default_port('redis')` returns 6379.

title: Video Game XP Level Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_player_level(xp)` that takes an integer XP and returns the player's level (1 through 9) using sequential conditional checks. The XP thresholds for levels 1 through 9 are: level 1 is default; level 2 requires 1000 XP; level 3 requires 2500 XP; level 4 requires 5000 XP; level 5 requires 10000 XP; level 6 requires 25000 XP; level 7 requires 50000 XP; level 8 requires 100000 XP; and level 9 requires 250000 XP. Return the highest level the player has achieved. Example: `get_player_level(5000)` returns 4.

title: Solar System Distances
spec: Create a function `get_orbital_distance_km(body_name)` that returns the approximate average distance from Earth in kilometers for various celestial bodies. Use an `if/elif` or `match` statement to map the following strictly to their integer values: 'Moon' -> 384400, 'Sun' -> 149597870, 'Mars' -> 54600000, 'Venus' -> 38000000, 'Mercury' -> 77000000, 'Jupiter' -> 588000000, 'Saturn' -> 1200000000, 'Neptune' -> 4500000000. Return -1 for unknown bodies. Example: `get_orbital_distance_km('Moon')` returns 384400.

title: Hardware Power States
spec: Implement a function `get_power_consumption_mw(state)` that returns the expected power draw in milliwatts for different hardware operational states. Map the following states to their exact integer values using an `if/elif` block: 'sleep_deep' -> 1500, 'sleep_light' -> 2500, 'idle' -> 12000, 'low_load' -> 35000, 'medium_load' -> 65000, 'high_load' -> 125000, 'peak_load' -> 250000, 'critical_threshold' -> 300000. Return 0 for unrecognized states. Example: `get_power_consumption_mw('idle')` returns 12000.

title: Bandwidth Allocator
spec: Write a function `get_allocated_kbps(plan_name)` that assigns network bandwidth in kilobits per second based on the user's subscription plan. Using a sequential conditional structure, return the following integer limits: 'basic_mobile' -> 1500, 'basic_desktop' -> 5000, 'standard_mobile' -> 12000, 'standard_desktop' -> 25000, 'premium_mobile' -> 50000, 'premium_desktop' -> 100000, 'gigabit_node' -> 1000000, 'backbone_link' -> 10000000. Fallback to 0 if the plan is unknown. Example: `get_allocated_kbps('standard_mobile')` returns 12000.

title: Geological Eras Validator
spec: Write a function `get_geological_epoch(years_ago)` that classifies a time period into a geological epoch based on the upper boundary in years before present. Using an `if/elif` chain from youngest to oldest, classify as follows: less than 11700 -> 'Holocene', less than 2580000 -> 'Pleistocene', less than 5330000 -> 'Pliocene', less than 23030000 -> 'Miocene', less than 33900000 -> 'Oligocene', less than 56000000 -> 'Eocene', less than 66000000 -> 'Paleocene', less than 145000000 -> 'Cretaceous'. Otherwise return 'Older'. Example: `get_geological_epoch(10000)` returns 'Holocene'.

title: Atmospheric Altitude Layers
spec: Create a function `get_atmospheric_layer(altitude_meters)` that returns the name of the atmospheric layer for a given altitude in meters. Use these upper limits sequentially via `if/elif`: under 12000 is 'Troposphere', under 35000 is 'Ozone Layer', under 50000 is 'Stratosphere', under 85000 is 'Mesosphere', under 100000 is 'Karman Line', under 408000 is 'ISS Orbit', under 600000 is 'Thermosphere', and under 10000000 is 'Exosphere'. Otherwise return 'Space'. Example: `get_atmospheric_layer(15000)` returns 'Ozone Layer'.

title: Loyalty Points Catalog
spec: Write a function `get_item_cost(item_name)` for an e-commerce rewards program. It must return the integer points cost for specific reward items. Implement this using an `if/elif` chain or `match` statement. Map 'Coffee Mug' to 1500, 'T-Shirt' to 3500, 'Hoodie' to 8500, 'Headphones' to 15000, 'Smartwatch' to 35000, 'Tablet' to 65000, 'Smartphone' to 120000, and 'Laptop' to 250000. Return 0 for unavailable items. Example: `get_item_cost('Hoodie')` returns 8500.

title: Urban Population Classifier
spec: Implement a function `classify_population(population_count)` that returns a string describing the settlement size. Evaluate sequentially using strict upper boundaries: less than 1000 is 'Hamlet', less than 5000 is 'Village', less than 20000 is 'Town', less than 100000 is 'Large Town', less than 500000 is 'City', less than 3000000 is 'Metropolis', less than 10000000 is 'Megacity'. For 10000000 or more, return 'Megalopolis'. Example: `classify_population(150000)` returns 'City'.

title: Logistics Freight Weights
spec: Write a function `get_freight_class(weight_grams)` that categorizes a package based on its weight in grams. Using sequential conditional checks, define the categories and their upper weight limits: under 1500 -> 'Small Parcel', under 5000 -> 'Medium Parcel', under 15000 -> 'Large Parcel', under 30000 -> 'Oversize', under 150000 -> 'Freight Pallet', under 500000 -> 'Heavy Freight', under 12000000 -> 'Container'. If 12000000 or more, return 'Ultra Heavy'. Example: `get_freight_class(2000)` returns 'Medium Parcel'.

title: Audio Equalizer Frequencies
spec: Create a function `get_center_frequency(band_name)` for a digital audio equalizer. Return the exact integer center frequency in Hertz for the following named bands using an `if/elif` mapping: 'Mid-Low' is 1500, 'Mid' is 2500, 'Upper-Mid' is 4000, 'High' is 7500, 'Presence' is 12000, 'Brilliance' is 16000, 'Ultra' is 22000, and 'Studio' is 96000. Return -1 for unknown bands. Example: `get_center_frequency('High')` returns 7500.

title: Unicode Block Starting Points
spec: Implement `get_unicode_block_start(block_name)` which returns the decimal integer starting codepoint for requested Unicode blocks. Use an `if/elif` structure to map the following strings: 'Hiragana' to 12352, 'Katakana' to 12448, 'Bopomofo' to 12544, 'Hangul Jamo' to 4352, 'CJK Unified' to 19968, 'Runic' to 5760, 'Khmer' to 6016, and 'Myanmar' to 4096. Return 0 if the block name is not recognized. Example: `get_unicode_block_start('Runic')` returns 5760.

title: Aircraft MTOW Classifier
spec: Write a function `get_max_takeoff_weight_kg(aircraft_class)` that maps a standard aircraft class string to its maximum takeoff weight in kilograms. Implement the mapping via an `if/elif` sequence. Return 2500 for 'Very Light', 5700 for 'Light', 45000 for 'Medium', 136000 for 'Heavy', 300000 for 'Super Heavy', 447000 for 'Jumbo', 575000 for 'Mega', and 640000 for 'Ultra'. For unknown classes, return 0. Example: `get_max_takeoff_weight_kg('Light')` returns 5700.

title: Hardware Memory Map
spec: Create a function `get_memory_region_start(region_name)` for a fantasy console emulator. It must return the integer decimal address where the requested region begins using an `if/elif` block. Map 'Boot ROM' to 65536, 'VRAM' to 131072, 'WRAM' to 262144, 'SRAM' to 524288, 'System Registers' to 1048576, 'Audio Registers' to 2097152, 'Expansion' to 4194304, and 'Interrupt Vector' to 8388608. Return -1 otherwise. Example: `get_memory_region_start('VRAM')` returns 131072.

title: Telescope Wavelength Bands
spec: Write `get_band_wavelength_angstroms(band_name)` which provides the typical wavelength in Angstroms for various astronomy observation bands. Use an `if/elif` or `match/case` block to map 'Ultraviolet' to 4000, 'Visible' to 7000, 'Near Infrared' to 25000, 'Mid Infrared' to 50000, 'Far Infrared' to 350000, 'Submillimeter' to 1000000, 'Microwave' to 10000000, and 'Radio' to 50000000. Return 0 for invalid bands. Example: `get_band_wavelength_angstroms('Visible')` returns 7000.

title: Corporate Service Bonus
spec: Write a function `calculate_service_bonus(years)` that returns a fixed dollar bonus based on an employee's years of service. Use a sequence of `if/elif` statements to map exactly 5 years to 2500, 10 years to 7500, 15 years to 15000, 20 years to 30000, 25 years to 50000, 30 years to 75000, 35 years to 125000, and 40 years to 250000. If the input does not perfectly match one of these milestones, return 0. Example: `calculate_service_bonus(20)` returns 30000.

title: Creator Play Button Awards
spec: Implement a function `get_award_subscribers(award_name)` that returns the number of subscribers required to receive a specific creator award. Use a sequence of conditional checks to map 'Graphite' to 1000, 'Opal' to 5000, 'Bronze' to 10000, 'Silver' to 100000, 'Emerald' to 250000, 'Gold' to 1000000, 'Ruby' to 5000000, and 'Diamond' to 10000000. Return 0 for unrecognized awards. Example: `get_award_subscribers('Silver')` returns 100000.

title: Time Conversions to Seconds
spec: Write a module with a function `get_seconds_in_period(period_name)` that returns the exact integer number of seconds in various time periods. Use an `if/elif` chain or sequential matching for the following standard durations: 'Hour' -> 3600, 'Day' -> 86400, 'Week' -> 604800, 'Standard Month' -> 2592000, 'Standard Year' -> 31536000, 'Leap Year' -> 31622400, 'Decade' -> 315360000, 'Century' -> 3153600000. Return 0 if the period is not recognized. Example: `get_seconds_in_period('Day')` returns 86400.

title: File Size Quotas
spec: Write a function `get_tier_quota_bytes(tier_name)` that sets file upload limits based on the user's account tier. Implement this logic sequentially with `if/elif` to map the tiers to their exact bytes limits: 'Guest' -> 1024000, 'Basic' -> 5120000, 'Standard' -> 10240000, 'Pro' -> 51200000, 'Premium' -> 256000000, 'Ultra' -> 1024000000, 'Enterprise' -> 5368709120, 'Admin' -> 10737418240. Return 0 for unknown tiers. Example: `get_tier_quota_bytes('Guest')` returns 1024000.

title: Transaction Limits
spec: Create a function `get_max_transaction_amount(account_type)` that returns the maximum allowed daily transaction amount in cents based on the account type. Use an `if/elif` chain for the mapping: map 'Student' to 2500, 'Basic' to 10000, 'Standard' to 25000, 'Plus' to 50000, 'Premium' to 100000, 'Business' to 250000, 'Corporate' to 1000000, and 'Institutional' to 5000000. Return 0 for unknown types. Example: `get_max_transaction_amount('Standard')` returns 25000.

title: Frequent Flyer Status
spec: Implement a function `get_frequent_flyer_status(miles)` that classifies a passenger's status based on their miles. Use a sequential `if/elif` chain from lowest to highest boundary. Under 25000 miles is 'Member', under 50000 is 'Silver', under 75000 is 'Gold', under 100000 is 'Platinum', under 150000 is 'Diamond', under 250000 is 'Diamond Plus', under 500000 is 'Global', and under 1000000 is 'Cosmic'. For 1000000 or more, return 'Cosmic Elite'. Example: `get_frequent_flyer_status(60000)` returns 'Gold'.

title: Credit Limit Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_base_credit_limit(profession)` that sets a default integer credit limit in dollars based on a stated profession string. Map the assignments using an `if/elif` structure: 'Doctor' -> 150000, 'Engineer' -> 120000, 'Teacher' -> 50000, 'Artist' -> 15000, 'Manager' -> 85000, 'Executive' -> 250000, 'Clerk' -> 12000, 'Student' -> 2500. Return 0 for unlisted professions. Example: `get_base_credit_limit('Teacher')` returns 50000.

title: Stock Exchange Listing Fees
spec: Write a function `get_listing_fee(exchange_code)` that returns the required baseline listing fee in dollars for various global stock exchanges. Use an `if/elif` or `match` statement to map 'NYSE' to 250000, 'NASDAQ' to 150000, 'LSE' to 120000, 'TSX' to 75000, 'ASX' to 50000, 'HKEX' to 200000, 'SGX' to 65000, and 'FRA' to 85000. If the exchange code is unknown, return -1. Example: `get_listing_fee('TSX')` returns 75000.

title: Charity Donation Tiers
spec: Create a function `get_donor_tier(donation_amount)` that assigns a title to a donor based on their total contribution. Evaluate strictly with sequential upper bounds: under 1000 is 'Supporter', under 2500 is 'Friend', under 5000 is 'Patron', under 10000 is 'Benefactor', under 25000 is 'Champion', under 50000 is 'Visionary', under 100000 is 'Philanthropist', and 100000 or more is 'Founder'. Example: `get_donor_tier(1500)` returns 'Friend'.

title: Social Media Base Reach Cap
spec: Implement a function `get_reach_cap(tier_name)` that returns the algorithmic base cap on post impressions for different influencer tiers. Implement this using an `if/elif` chain to map the tier strings to these integer caps: 'Nano' -> 1500, 'Micro' -> 3500, 'Small' -> 8500, 'Medium' -> 15000, 'Large' -> 25000, 'Macro' -> 100000, 'Mega' -> 150000, and 'Giga' -> 500000. Return 0 for invalid tiers. Example: `get_reach_cap('Small')` returns 8500.

title: Standard Resistor Value Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_resistor(ohms: int) -> str` that categorizes resistance into specific bins based on exact standard values. Return "1k" for exactly 1000, "2.2k" for exactly 2200, "3.3k" for exactly 3300, "4.7k" for exactly 4700, "6.8k" for exactly 6800, "10k" for exactly 10000, "22k" for exactly 22000, and "47k" for exactly 47000. For any other values, return "Non-standard". Write a helper function `is_high_resistance(ohms: int) -> bool` that returns True if the resistance is at least 10000. Example: classify_resistor(4700) -> "4.7k".

title: Industrial Motor RPM Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze_motor_speed(rpm: int) -> str` that maps a given exact RPM to its industrial classification. Exactly 1200 returns "Low Speed Six-Pole". Exactly 1500 returns "Fifty-Hz Four-Pole". Exactly 1800 returns "Sixty-Hz Four-Pole". Exactly 3000 returns "Fifty-Hz Two-Pole". Exactly 3600 returns "Sixty-Hz Two-Pole". Exactly 7200 returns "High Speed". Exactly 10000 returns "Very High Speed". Exactly 15000 returns "Ultra High Speed". Exactly 24000 returns "Extreme Speed". For anything else, return "Unclassified". Example: analyze_motor_speed(3600) -> "Sixty-Hz Two-Pole".

title: Infrared Spectrum Band Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_ir_band(nanometers: int) -> str` that categorizes infrared light based on its wavelength in nanometers using sequential upper bounds. If the wavelength is less than 1000, return "Near IR One". If less than 1400, return "Near IR Two". If less than 3000, return "Short Wavelength IR". If less than 5000, return "Mid Wavelength IR". If less than 8000, return "Long Wavelength IR One". If less than 15000, return "Long Wavelength IR Two". If less than 30000, return "Far IR One". If less than 100000, return "Far IR Two". Anything higher is "Terahertz". Example: classify_ir_band(2500) -> "Short Wavelength IR".

title: Global Railway Gauge Classifier
spec: Write a module with a function `classify_gauge(mm: int) -> str` that takes a railway track gauge in millimeters and returns its common name. Check for these exact values: 1000 returns "Meter", 1067 returns "CAPE", 1435 returns "Standard", 1520 returns "Russian", 1524 returns "Iberian Early", 1600 returns "Irish", 1668 returns "Iberian", and 1676 returns "Indian". If the gauge does not match any of these exactly, return "Non-standard". Include a driver function `filter_standard(gauges: list[int]) -> list[str]` that processes a list of gauges. Example: classify_gauge(1435) -> "Standard".

title: National Income Tax Threshold Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_bracket_threshold(level: int) -> int` that returns the maximum income threshold for a given tax bracket level in a simplified national system. Level 1 returns 11000. Level 2 returns 44725. Level 3 returns 95375. Level 4 returns 182100. Level 5 returns 231250. Level 6 returns 323925. Level 7 returns 431900. Level 8 returns 578125. For any other level, return 9999999. Write a second function `is_high_income(income: int) -> bool` that returns True if the income strictly exceeds the level 5 threshold. Example: get_bracket_threshold(3) -> 95375.

title: Vehicle Maintenance Schedule Generator
spec: Write a function `get_maintenance_tasks(mileage: int) -> list[str]` that returns a list of required maintenance tasks for a given vehicle mileage. Add "Oil Change" to the list if mileage is an exact multiple of 5000. Add "Tire Rotation" if a multiple of 15000. Add "Air Filter" if a multiple of 30000. Add "Spark Plugs" if a multiple of 60000. Add "Timing Belt" if a multiple of 100000. Add "Coolant Flush" if a multiple of 150000. Add "Transmission Fluid" if a multiple of 250000. Add "Engine Overhaul" if a multiple of 500000. Example: get_maintenance_tasks(30000) -> ["Oil Change", "Tire Rotation", "Air Filter"].

title: Digital Sensor Megapixel Tiering
spec: Write a function `get_sensor_tier(total_pixels: int) -> str` that categorizes a camera sensor based on its total pixel count using sequential upper limits. Under 1000000 is "Sub-Megapixel". Up to 2000000 is "Basic Class". Up to 5000000 is "Standard Class". Up to 8000000 is "High Def Class". Up to 12000000 is "Standard Mobile". Up to 24000000 is "Standard Format". Up to 45000000 is "High-Res Format". Up to 100000000 is "Medium Format". Anything strictly greater is "Large Format". Example: get_sensor_tier(15000000) -> "Standard Format".

title: Digital Camera ISO Classifier
spec: Write a function `evaluate_iso_noise(iso: int) -> str` that assesses expected sensor noise for specific exact high ISO speeds. Return "Very Clean" for exactly 1600. Return "Clean" for exactly 3200. Return "Slight Noise" for exactly 6400. Return "Noticeable" for exactly 12800. Return "Noisy" for exactly 25600. Return "Severe" for exactly 51200. Return "Unusable" for exactly 102400. Return "Extreme" for exactly 204800. For any other ISO input, return "Unknown". Example: evaluate_iso_noise(6400) -> "Slight Noise".

title: Public Sector Salary Band Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_salary_band(salary: int) -> str` that classifies a salary into predefined public sector bands using sequential upper limits. Less than 35000 is "Band A", up to 45000 is "Band B", up to 60000 is "Band C", up to 85000 is "Band D", up to 120000 is "Band E", up to 150000 is "Band F", up to 200000 is "Band G", and up to 250000 is "Band H". Anything higher is "Executive". Include a driver function `process_salaries(salaries: list[int]) -> dict` that counts how many salaries fall into each band. Example: get_salary_band(55000) -> "Band C".

title: Streaming Video Bitrate Optimizer
spec: Write a function `recommend_quality(bitrate_kbps: int) -> str` that recommends the streaming video preset suitable for a given network bitrate in kbps. Evaluate sequentially: less than 1500 returns "Low Quality", up to 2500 returns "Standard Def", up to 4500 returns "Enhanced Def", up to 8000 returns "High Def", up to 12000 returns "Full Def", up to 16000 returns "Quad Def", up to 35000 returns "Ultra Def", and up to 68000 returns "Hyper Def". Above that returns "Uncompressed". Example: recommend_quality(6000) -> "High Def".

title: Chess Federation Title Assigner
spec: Write a function `get_chess_title(elo: int) -> str` that assigns a chess title based on Elo rating thresholds, checked sequentially. Return "Novice" for ratings below 1200, "Class C" for up to 1400, "Class B" for up to 1600, "Class A" for up to 1800, "Candidate Master" for up to 2000, "National Master" for up to 2200, "International Master" for up to 2400, "Grandmaster" for up to 2500, and "Elite Grandmaster" for ratings up to 2700. Above that is "Super Grandmaster". Example: get_chess_title(2300) -> "International Master".

title: CBC Hematology Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze_wbc(count: int) -> str` that evaluates a white blood cell count (cells per microliter) sequentially. Below 1000 is "Severe Deficit", below 3000 is "Moderate Deficit", below 4000 is "Mild Deficit", up to 11000 is "Normal", up to 25000 is "Mild Excess", up to 50000 is "Moderate Excess", and up to 100000 is "Severe Excess". Above 100000 is "Critical". Also write `analyze_platelets(count: int) -> str` returning "Low" below 150000, "Normal" up to 450000, and "High" above. Example: analyze_wbc(6000) -> "Normal".

title: Horology Beat Rate Converter
spec: Write a function `classify_beat_rate(vph: int) -> str` that takes a mechanical watch's vibrations per hour (vph) and returns its common horological classification using exact mappings. Exactly 14400 returns "Slow Beat". Exactly 18000 returns "Traditional". Exactly 21600 returns "Modern Slow". Exactly 25200 returns "Specialized Escapement". Exactly 28800 returns "Modern Standard". Exactly 36000 returns "High Beat". Exactly 72000 returns "Ultra High Beat". Exactly 360000 returns "Precision Chronograph". Return "Unknown" otherwise. Example: classify_beat_rate(28800) -> "Modern Standard".

title: Used Car Value Depreciator
spec: Write a function `get_depreciation_factor(mileage: int) -> float` that returns a multiplier for a used car's base value based on its mileage sequentially. Less than 10000 miles returns 0.95, up to 20000 is 0.85, up to 30000 is 0.75, up to 40000 is 0.65, up to 50000 is 0.55, up to 60000 is 0.45, up to 70000 is 0.35, up to 80000 is 0.25, up to 90000 is 0.15, and up to 100000 is 0.10. Over 100000 returns 0.05. Example: get_depreciation_factor(45000) -> 0.55.

title: Literary Genre Word Count Validator
spec: Write a function `categorize_manuscript(word_count: int) -> str` that classifies a manuscript based on its length sequentially. Less than 1000 is "Flash Fiction", up to 7500 is "Short Story", up to 10000 is "Long Short Story", up to 17500 is "Novelette", up to 40000 is "Novella", up to 80000 is "Novel", up to 110000 is "Epic", and up to 150000 is "Massive Tome". Anything higher is "Saga". Also write `check_challenge_winner(word_count: int) -> bool` which returns True if the count is at least 50000. Example: categorize_manuscript(25000) -> "Novella".

title: Egyptian Dynasty Chronology Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_kingdom(year_bce: int) -> str` that maps a year BCE to a major period in Ancient Egypt using sequential bounds. If greater than 10000, return "Paleolithic". If at least 3100, return "Prehistoric". If at least 2686, return "Early Dynastic". If at least 2181, return "Old Kingdom". If at least 2055, return "First Intermediate". If at least 1650, return "Middle Kingdom". If at least 1550, return "Second Intermediate". If at least 1189, return "Ramesside Period". If at least 1069, return "New Kingdom". Return "Late Period" for lower years. Example: get_kingdom(2500) -> "Old Kingdom".

title: Eight-Thousander Summit Identifier
spec: Write a function `identify_peak(elevation_meters: int) -> str` that identifies a specific Himalayan peak given its exact official elevation in meters. Map the exact values: 8848 to "Everest", 8611 to "K-Two", 8586 to "Kangchenjunga", 8516 to "Lhotse", 8485 to "Makalu", 8188 to "Cho Oyu", 8167 to "Dhaulagiri", 8163 to "Manaslu", 8126 to "Nanga Parbat", and 8091 to "Annapurna". Return "Other" for any other input. Example: identify_peak(8611) -> "K-Two".

title: Camera Exposure Speed Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_shutter_speed(microseconds: int) -> str` that categorizes a shutter speed duration. Map exactly 1000 to "Action Freezing", 2000 to "Sports Action", 4000 to "Fast Motion", 8000 to "Handheld Telephoto", 16667 to "Standard Handheld", 33333 to "Slow Handheld", 66667 to "Motion Blur", 125000 to "Flowing Water", 250000 to "Night Scene", and 500000 to "Long Exposure". Return "Custom" for any other values. Example: classify_shutter_speed(4000) -> "Fast Motion".

title: Portable Power Bank Flight Regulator
spec: Write a function `check_battery_allowance(capacity_mah: int) -> str` that categorizes a battery for air travel based on capacity bounds sequentially. Less than 2000 is "Micro", up to 5000 is "Small", up to 10000 is "Medium", up to 20000 is "Large", up to 27000 is "Max Standard", up to 32000 is "Requires Airline Approval", up to 40000 is "Cargo Only", up to 50000 is "Ground Transport", and above 50000 is "Prohibited". Also write `is_high_capacity(capacity: int) -> bool` returning True if capacity is at least 20000. Example: check_battery_allowance(15000) -> "Large".

title: Ancient City Population Analyzer
spec: Write a function `classify_city_size(population: int) -> str` that categorizes the scale of historical ancient cities based on estimated population sequentially. Returns "Hamlet" for under 1000, "Village" for up to 5000, "Town" for up to 15000, "City" for up to 40000, "Large City" for up to 100000, "Metropolis" for up to 250000, "Megacity" for up to 500000, and "Empire Capital" for up to 1000000. Anything greater is "Unprecedented". Example: classify_city_size(120000) -> "Metropolis".

title: East Coast Zip Code Router
spec: Write a function `route_package(zip_code: int) -> str` that assigns a package to an East Coast distribution hub based on its zip code sequentially. If the zip code is less than 10000, return "Invalid". If less than 15000, return "Hub NY". If less than 20000, return "Hub PA". If less than 20600, return "Hub DC". If less than 22000, return "Hub MD". If less than 24700, return "Hub VA". If less than 27000, return "Hub WV". If less than 29000, return "Hub NC". Otherwise, return "Out of Zone". Example: route_package(21050) -> "Hub MD".

title: Retro Computer Memory Mapper
spec: Write a function `get_system_ram(bytes_val: int) -> str` that identifies classic eight-bit and sixteen-bit computers based on their exact standard RAM configurations in bytes. Map 4096 to "VIC Basic", 8192 to "Atari Early", 16384 to "Spectrum Basic", 32768 to "BBC Micro", 49152 to "Atari Late", 65536 to "Commodore Edition", 131072 to "Apple Extended", and 524288 to "Amiga Basic". Return "Unknown System" otherwise. Example: get_system_ram(65536) -> "Commodore Edition".

title: Volcanic Explosivity Index Estimator
spec: Write a function `estimate_vei(volume_cubic_meters: int) -> int` that returns the Volcanic Explosivity Index (VEI) based on the volume of ejecta sequentially. A volume less than 10000 is VEI 0. Up to 1000000 is VEI 1. Up to 10000000 is VEI 2. Up to 100000000 is VEI 3. Up to 1000000000 is VEI 4. Up to 10000000000 is VEI 5. Up to 100000000000 is VEI 6. Up to 1000000000000 is VEI 7. Above that is VEI 8. Example: estimate_vei(50000000) -> 3.

title: Ship Gross Tonnage Classifier
spec: Write a function `classify_vessel(tonnage: int) -> str` that categorizes commercial ships based on their Gross Tonnage thresholds sequentially. Under 1000 is "Small Craft", up to 10000 is "Coastal Freighter", up to 25000 is "Handysize", up to 50000 is "Handymax", up to 80000 is "Panamax", up to 120000 is "Aframax", up to 160000 is "Suezmax", up to 320000 is "Very Large Carrier", and anything strictly above is "Ultra Large Carrier". Example: classify_vessel(60000) -> "Panamax".

title: Diamond Cent-Pricing Appraiser
spec: Write a function `get_base_price_cents(carat_points: int) -> int` that evaluates a baseline price in cents for a flawless diamond based on its weight sequentially. If points < 25, return 1500; if < 50, return 4500; if < 75, return 9500; if < 100, return 18000; if < 150, return 35000; if < 200, return 65000; if < 300, return 120000; and if < 400, return 250000. For 400 or more, return 500000. Example: get_base_price_cents(60) -> 9500.

title: Concrete Compressive Strength Classifier
spec: Write a module with a function `classify_concrete(psi: int) -> str` that categorizes concrete based on its compressive strength in PSI. title: Animal Daily Maintenance Calories
spec: Create a veterinary nutrition calculator that returns the average daily maintenance calories (in kcal) for large and exotic animals. Write a function `get_maintenance_kcal(animal_name: str) -> int` with the following distinct mappings: 'Cheetah' (2000), 'Human' (2200), 'Gorilla' (4000), 'Lion' (6000), 'Tiger' (8000), 'Polar Bear' (12000), 'Horse' (15000), 'Walrus' (25000), 'Elephant' (70000), 'Humpback Whale' (200000), 'Orca' (250000), 'Fin Whale' (300000), and 'Blue Whale' (500000). If the animal is not found, return 0. Include a simple main block to print the caloric needs of a 'Gorilla' and an 'Elephant'.
